races.name: Title Sponsor Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has failed to win or place on good ground in recent outings (0W 0P from 4 runs on similar going), and carries a tongue-tie; shapes as a solid position-holder but her recent form offers limited encouragement even if she lands the right tactical spot.
runners_data.comment: This mare failed to see out an even longer trip when well beaten at Hamilton last time, but today's shorter test sits closer to her ideal range of 8 to 11 furlongs. She's had her share of issues and is without a win in her last four starts, so proof of ability is needed before she can be trusted, with a rating of 66 reflecting a modest look on paper.

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: Has a solitary win and one placing from 15 runs on similar going, which tempers expectations, but Cara Tuke claims 5lb and Iain Jardine sends out horses in form (T14: 4/38); will look to press from a prominent position but struggles to convert.
runners_data.comment: This gelding's rating of 79 puts him third best of this field on pure figures, making him hard to ignore if he can rediscover his level. He's been below par of late, down the field in a handicap at York most recently, with his official mark easing as a result; he stays 11 furlongs but could even be better suited by a shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a 316-day absence — a significant fitness flag — and although her form before the break included back-to-back thirds on good ground over suitable distances, asking her to land a blow fresh off such a long layoff is a major ask; Lexie Clarkson claims 5lb.
runners_data.comment: A filly who has been off the track for the best part of a year, she ran to her level when beaten three lengths off a 3lb higher mark at Killarney in August, her sole start since, and manifestly needs the run following such a lengthy absence. Effective from 10 to 12 furlongs and rated only 67, she's up against it fresh on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who showed a good second last time on soft ground and has placed twice on similar going from 15 attempts; Josephine Gordon is the standout jockey booking in this field, and he handles a range of distances — the concern is that an uncontested Krissy won't generate enough pace to bring him into it.
runners_data.comment: Back in form across both codes recently, this gelding ranks second on our figures at a rating of 82 and remains a serious threat. The query is more about conditions than ability: he already seemed to want a tougher test when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a 1lb lower mark at Ayr last time, and today's shorter trip, well inside his best of two miles, could be on the sharp side for him.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and clear race-shaper, with four wins in nine good-going runs and a recent double win at 9f; STYLE_FIT flag notes she is technically operating out of a natural prominent-press role into a full lead here, but her recent form is by far the most compelling in the field and she controls the tactical keys.
runners_data.comment: This mare boasts three wins in her last six starts, including a half-length success at Musselburgh last time when allowed an uncontested lead off a 3lb lower mark. She needs to dictate from the front to be seen at her best, which could be the deciding factor from stall three, but on form figures alone she's a leading threat at a rating of 78.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a hood, who has finished in the top five in each of the last five starts on good ground (0W 2P); Tim Easterby sends this one out freshened after just 10 days and the 12 runs on similar going give him a solid data set, though lack of a strong pace is his biggest enemy.
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency without a win in his last five starts, this gelding ran to par when beaten three lengths off a 1lb higher mark here last time, and he races for a yard with an excellent record at the course. First-time blinkers may sharpen him up further, and with this trip suiting, he's rated 73 and worth another chance.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Comes into this off an eight-day break with a win and a second in her last two starts, both on good ground at 8-9f; she has a 1W 4P record from 15 similar-going runs, which underlines her consistency, and Joanna Mason is a capable jockey for this type — she wants to be prominent and the trip stepping up to 1m1f is the one query.
runners_data.comment: In excellent form, this gelding made smooth headway from off the pace to win with a little in hand here last time, doing so from a mark 3lb lower than he carries today. Versatile on ground and effective from 6 to 9 furlongs, he's rated 83, right at the head of this field on figures, with the only query being whether he repeats that same finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: In truth a front-to-prominent runner who is placed into a midfield mapping here because the prominent slots are congested; Laura Pearson takes the ride and she has placed three times in recent starts without winning, making her a place contender rather than a likely winner even if she sneaks a forward position.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts but continuing to build towards his peak, this gelding was beaten only half a length off a 1lb lower mark here last time, with his current mark now more workable for him. He can be fractious beforehand, but with the yard in form and conditions to suit at 8 to 9 furlongs, he's rated 71 and capable of featuring.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: This 11-year-old is at heart a prominent racer — the mapping to midfield reflects an overcrowded front end rather than his natural instinct; Miss Rebecca Burley (5lb) claims the ride for Easterby's stable, and while he has veteran course craft, his recent string of poor finishes (8th, 4th, 7th, 11th, 9th) makes it hard to see him reversing the trend.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten when dropped to a mile in a handicap here last time, this gelding remains without a win in his last five starts and sits bottom of these figures on a rating of 64. His only worthwhile effort recently came in a race for apprentice riders, and he needs plenty to turn around at this level even with today's trip back in his 8-10f range.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy is the confirmed pace-setter and, with no other genuine front-runner to pressure her, she is almost certain to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo on this Good to Firm Carlisle surface over 1m1f. Kisiyra and Izzari are the natural prominent horses who will look to sit just off Krissy's shoulder, while Hostility — coming off a recent win and a runner-up — has the profile to also press for an early position, creating a modestly competitive early stretch but nothing chaotic. The hold-up horses Mr Lincoln, Eagles Dream, and Financer will be operating from the rear, needing a strong enough pace to bring them into it late, which an uncontested Krissy is unlikely to provide. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Bellasio and Jewel Maker are genuine front-to-prominent runners redistributed to midfield, and Krissy and Kisiyra are most likely to lock out the favoured early slots. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently and travel into the contest without expending energy fighting for position — prominent racers with recent good form and tactical speed hold the clear advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krissy Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy leads uncontested and sets a measured tempo that leaves the hold-up horses with insufficient cover to close.
scenarios.body: If Krissy leads uncontested and sets a measured tempo that leaves the hold-up horses with insufficient cover to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Grinds Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy sets a surprisingly strong gallop — perhaps pressed more than expected — and the race truly tests stamina over this 1m1f trip.
scenarios.body: If Krissy sets a surprisingly strong gallop — perhaps pressed more than expected — and the race truly tests stamina over this 1m1f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If Bellasio or Jewel Maker win the early battle for position and their natural prominent style reasserts despite the redistribution.
scenarios.body: If Bellasio or Jewel Maker win the early battle for position and their natural prominent style reasserts despite the redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Krissy Fades, Wide-Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy's recent busy schedule catches up with her and she sets a pace she cannot sustain, leaving a contest that collapses into a scramble.
scenarios.body: If Krissy's recent busy schedule catches up with her and she sets a pace she cannot sustain, leaving a contest that collapses into a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Krissy's pace: if she bowls along uncontested, watch whether Kisiyra and Izzari can maintain contact around the turn — if they drop away, the race could be over bar the shouting inside the final furlong.

Eagles Dream's fitness: 316 days off means her first-time-back readiness is unverified — if she travels sweetly early she may be fitter than the layoff suggests, but watch for her dropping away quickly if the race develops with any tempo.

Bellasio and Jewel Maker scrambling for position: both are natural prominent types crammed into a midfield role — if either bustles forward aggressively in the first furlong and disrupts the expected order, the early pace dynamic could shift unpredictably.

Mr Lincoln's jockey advantage: Josephine Gordon is the highest-profile rider in this field and if Mr Lincoln gets a decent split at the two-furlong marker, watch whether she can pick off tired prominent horses — this is the most realistic hold-up threat.

Going confirmation: the race card lists Good but the going report repeatedly confirms Good to Firm — if the ground is riding faster than billed, Krissy's front-running supremacy is reinforced and hold-up horses face an even stiffer ask closing from off the pace.

races.name: Style Awards Fashion Finale Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type trained by James Owen who handles Good ground well (4/15 on similar) and has course-and-distance experience, though at 9 and carrying 144lbs over a mile this trip is on the sharp side; placed twice from similar going, could stay on without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Faded from the front rank to finish fourth, beaten eight lengths, unable to last home over a testing mile and a quarter at Pontefract last time. A drop back to today's sharper trip, alongside the addition of a tongue-tie and visor, could bring a much-needed leap forward, and he's without a win in his last six starts but rates a solid fourth on our figures at 52.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old has placed on Good ground at shorter trips but her recent form includes a string of poor finishes on Soft and Standard; a natural hold-up horse pushed further forward than she'd like by the field shape, which erodes her chance in this low-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Performed to expectation when runner-up, beaten a length and a half off a marginally lower mark at Catterick last time, dropped in trip to 7f that day. Stepping back up to today's mile suits her proven range, and on a fair weight she sits mid-field on our figures at 51, still without a win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Captain Pickles
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner trained by Tony Culhane and Stella Barclay, last ran 54 days ago which is a notable absence; has form figures of 1-1-1 at shorter trips on Standard but this Good to Firm ground and a mile test on the flat represent genuine question marks over her stamina and going preference.
runners_data.comment: A below-par third, beaten seven lengths in a handicap at Wolverhampton, was the exception in an otherwise consistent campaign that had brought three wins from his previous five starts. Fifty-four days off since, but proven over today's trip and going, he's only mid-pack on our figures at 49 pending a return closer to his best.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this prominent-style six-year-old who has finished placed in several recent starts and handles a range of trips from 8-10f; no win on Good ground in the last five but her positional profile directly suits a race where only one other runner wants the front.
runners_data.comment: Twice a runner-up among his last six starts and still without a win, he found turf tougher going when beaten seven lengths in a handicap at Hamilton last time, a below-par run after some good form on the all-weather. First-time cheekpieces are added as he continues to search for that first solid effort on grass, and he rates second in our figures on 63 despite the query over the surface.

runners_data.name: Mertoun
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old landed her last start over 8f on Good and has placed twice more on the same going, giving the strongest recent form-and-going profile in the field; Alexandra Egan in the saddle, hold-up style but short odds to be closer given the field configuration.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by five and a half lengths at Windsor last time when pushed out, doing so with perhaps a bit more in hand than the bare result suggests off a mark ten pounds lower than today's. With the yard in good form and effective at today's trip and ground, he tops our figures on 65 and rates the one to beat, even up in the weights after that success.

runners_data.name: Top Gun Tina
runners_data.note: David Thompson runner who has finished no better than fourth in her last six, entirely on Standard ground; genuine late-runner type who has been mapped to midfield by necessity but is likely to find the pace shape and Good to Firm conditions conspiring against her natural waiting tactics.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency at this level, she matched that level when fourth, beaten three and a quarter lengths off a marginally higher mark at Newcastle last time. Well suited by today's trip, but she is having her first run in 75 days, and rates third in our figures on 58 among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Crumpet
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a recent 0 (pulled up/fell) and a string of finishes in the 7-11 range; a natural hold-up horse whose recent Carlisle record on Good ground is limited, and Lexie Clarkson claiming 3lb helps the weight but this mare's form makes her tough to side with regardless of position.
runners_data.comment: Question marks over stamina were raised when well beaten down the field over 10f in a classified event at Newcastle last time, extending a spell out of sorts without a win in her last six starts. First-time cheekpieces and a return to a sharper trip on today's ground, which she has raced over before, offer some hope of a bounce, but she's only seventh on our figures at 43.

runners_data.name: Shoptilyoudrop
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's four-year-old has not won and has a form string that trends downward from 4th to 8th; her true preference is for a waiting ride but in this congested field she will likely find herself racing further forward than ideal, which based on recent evidence is unlikely to unlock improvement.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten fifth when dropped to 6f in a handicap at Hamilton last time continued a run without a win in her last five starts, with her only form of real note coming on synthetic ground. Up in trip again today, beyond the 7f she seems to prefer, she sits towards the bottom of our figures on 40 and has plenty to find before she can feature.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's lightly-raced three-year-old carries the lowest weight (131lbs) and has a handful of Good-ground runs, finishing 6th and 4th on the going; a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield by field dynamics, young and lightly framed which could mean she runs on without the tactical advantage she'd need.
runners_data.comment: Never able to threaten before being eased down well beaten in a handicap at Musselburgh last time, he's shown little to suggest a change in fortunes across his last five starts. First-time cheekpieces are the obvious card to play, but he anchors our figures at 39 and has plenty to find on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — no race-day relevance; prior form shows repeated 8th-place finishes on Good ground over 8f but this entry is void.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Pickles is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, will slide into an uncontested lead on the Carlisle mile on Good to Firm ground and dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo. Book Of Life is the only other confirmed prominent runner and will likely slot into second behind Captain Pickles, meaning the pace duo shape the race without pressure from the rear. The field carries a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Wheres The Crumpet, Top Gun Tina, Shoptilyoudrop, Sanny Doo and Misemerald are all genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all race from the rear in practice; several will be forced wider or into a more prominent berth than they'd choose. A controlled, unchallenged gallop on fast ground over a flat mile strongly favours runners who can race prominently or in midfield and sustain their effort to the line, with Mertoun — who showed a strong last-run win over similar ground and distance — ideally placed to benefit; true closers are disadvantaged because the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Captain Pickles Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Pickles leads unchallenged and sets an honest but comfortable pace that stretches runners without collapsing.
scenarios.body: If Captain Pickles leads unchallenged and sets an honest but comfortable pace that stretches runners without collapsing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mertoun Powers Through
scenarios.trigger: If Mertoun travels strongly in midfield and produces her recent winning form to pick up decisively in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Mertoun travels strongly in midfield and produces her recent winning form to pick up decisively in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Pickles goes too fast early and fades, opening the race to a horse from slightly further back who travels well within herself.
scenarios.body: If Captain Pickles goes too fast early and fades, opening the race to a horse from slightly further back who travels well within herself.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure their preferred late-running position despite the field dynamics.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong and one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure their preferred late-running position despite the field dynamics.

watchPoints.text: Captain Pickles has not run for 54 days and her Standard-ground form may not transfer to Good to Firm — monitor her pre-race condition and if she shows any signs of rustiness at the start, her uncontested lead advantage becomes less bankable.

Mertoun is the standout on form and going but is a hold-up type by nature; watch how Alexandra Egan positions her in the early stages — if the field bunches and she gets trapped wide, she loses the positional edge that her profile requires.

Wheres The Crumpet posted a 0 in her last start and carries significant doubt around her well-being; if she drifts markedly in the market or shows any pre-race signs of unsettlement, treat as a non-factor regardless of market position.

Book Of Life is the most likely horse to press Captain Pickles into an honest gallop — if Joanna Mason elects to sit closer than expected, watch whether the pace quickens meaningfully at halfway, which would reorder the finish significantly.

The Good to Firm ground report is consistent across all races at Carlisle today; horses with Standard-ground form (Captain Pickles, Top Gun Tina, Shoptilyoudrop) face a genuine surface question that the market may not fully price in.

races.name: Sheila Petch Appreciation Handicap (For Professional Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Bravo Zulu
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose recent form includes a placed effort at 6f on Good ground; David Loughnane's yard is in decent nick (T14: 3/22) and the step back to 1m could help given an eighth-place run at this trip previously, but Laura Pearson will need pace to aim at from the back.
runners_data.comment: In and out of form across six starts, this gelding was about right when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a higher mark at Newmarket last time. He's proven at today's trip and ground, and a first-time eyeshield may add consistency, but needs more to feature prominently.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for K R Burke (T14: 8/45 is solid) who showed placed form at 8f on Standside going; Taryn Langley claims 5lb which is a notable advantage at this level, and securing a position just off Calyxoh early is the key to her chance.
runners_data.comment: Consistent with three places in his recent starts, this gelding was about right when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a higher mark at York last time. He's proven over today's trip and ground and ranks second of seven on our figures, but is yet to turn the form into a win.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will dictate terms uncontested; her recent form figures are poor (9-12-9-11 in last four) but her sole win came from a prominent position and she gets a soft lead here which flatters her chance, though a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is a mild flag for her prominence being slightly forced.
runners_data.comment: An indifferent spell continues, following a below-form run in Dubai with an eighth-length defeat in a Chester handicap last time. He does have today's trip and ground covered, though, and first-time cheekpieces offer hope for the outsider of this field.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Forward-going type for Jim Goldie (T14: 9/46) who has nine placed efforts at 8f on Good ground in her last five — this trip and going suit — but she has a 0 win-rate on similar going and will need to be sharper than her 097848 form string suggests.
runners_data.comment: Ranked third of seven on our figures and clear of her official mark, with form over today's trip and ground. She can carry her head high under pressure and was a shade below form at York last time, but on a sounder round she's the danger here.

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this six-year-old who is a natural prominent racer; he is mapped to midfield because the field is too crowded at the front for him to take his preferred berth, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 his chance is tempered if he cannot get forward — his best recent runs have come over 7f on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: An improved effort when beaten 7 lengths in a Newmarket handicap last time suggests this gelding is finding form again, having slipped below the mark that once brought success. He's effective at today's trip and ground, ranks fourth of seven on our figures, but still has a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: The Green Man
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon's mount is a genuine front-runner or close-up type by nature, forced back on the pace map by the volume of prominent horses in this field; his Good to Firm course figures are thin (2/15 sim-going) and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 underlines the concern that racing out of his natural role blunts his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the frame with three thirds and a second from six runs, this gelding ran close to form when beaten 2 lengths off a higher mark at Doncaster last time. He's proven at today's trip and tries a first-time tongue-tie and visor, though he's near bottom on our figures.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has five placed efforts from five runs at 8f on Good ground — a model of consistency — and Faye McManoman keeps the ride; headgear (p) is a positive flag and the 10-day turnaround for an in-form yard (T14: 14/100) is encouraging, but from a hold-up position she needs the pace to be genuine.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures, this gelding confirmed his consistency when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a lower mark at this course last time. From a yard with a fine record here and sporting first-time cheekpieces, he's the one to beat, though he must finally turn those places into a win.

races.paceDynamic: Calyxoh is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals likely to dispute the lead, will be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over this flat Carlisle mile. Inspired and Jannas Journey will push forward to try to claim prominent positions just off the pace, while Benacre and The Green Man — both natural prominent types — are displaced into midfield on the map because this field carries more forward-going horses than the race shape can accommodate at the front; Benacre and Inspired look most likely to actually secure the prominent berths given their consistent forward positioning, with The Green Man potentially squeezed back against his will. Bravo Zulu and Barley will operate from hold-up positions, relying on the pace being sufficient to close into at the business end. A single front-runner setting a sustainable but uncontested tempo on fast ground over a flat mile strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the gallop and produce a sustained finish — pure closers are unlikely to generate enough momentum to pick up ground in time.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Calyxoh Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Calyxoh dictates a clean, uncontested lead and the pace is honest but not punishing, allowing prominent stalkers to pounce off the final bend.
scenarios.body: If Calyxoh dictates a clean, uncontested lead and the pace is honest but not punishing, allowing prominent stalkers to pounce off the final bend.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Calyxoh's uncontested lead allows her to conserve enough energy to hold on in a truly end-to-end gallop that suits a front-runner stealing an unassailable lead.
scenarios.body: If Calyxoh's uncontested lead allows her to conserve enough energy to hold on in a truly end-to-end gallop that suits a front-runner stealing an unassailable lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle stages and Calyxoh's lack of competition causes her to back off, creating a truly strung-out race where closers suddenly find a wall of pace to aim at.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the middle stages and Calyxoh's lack of competition causes her to back off, creating a truly strung-out race where closers suddenly find a wall of pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Shape, Market Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling between the displaced prominent types (Benacre, The Green Man) and the legitimate front rank creates unexpected early pressure on Calyxoh and an uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: If early jostling between the displaced prominent types (Benacre, The Green Man) and the legitimate front rank creates unexpected early pressure on Calyxoh and an uneven gallop.

watchPoints.text: Inspired and Benacre may clash for the same prominent berth approaching the first bend — watch for early jostling that could unsettle both runners and scramble the anticipated race shape.

Calyxoh's recent form (9-12-9-11) is alarming and if she weakens sharply turning for home despite dictating terms, the race could devolve into a sprint for closers — monitor how she travels at the 3f pole.

The Green Man is a natural front-runner being pushed into midfield against his instincts; Josephine Gordon may attempt to push forward from the gate regardless, which could inject unexpected early pressure on Calyxoh and alter the entire pace scenario.

Barley's five placed efforts at 8f on Good ground make her a model of consistent placed form, but she has yet to win on similar going in her last 15 runs — watch whether she finishes strongly without quite getting there again.
Taryn Langley's 5lb claim on Inspired is the most significant weight advantage in the race and could prove decisive if the pace dynamic sets up for a forward-tracking horse in the final furlong.

races.name: Helen Stewart Appreciation Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Junkyard Dog
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has placed once over 15f on similar going; Cara Tuke claims 5lb which matters in a handicap, but the horse's recent form string of 5-4-5-8-9 shows a declining trajectory and this field is competitive enough to expose that.|
runners_data.comment: Well held in a handicap last time after switching back from hurdling, this gelding remains without a win having managed no better than 9th, 8th, 5th, 4th and 5th in recent starts. A first-time visor and a yard in good form offer a glimmer of hope, but rated only 57 off a mark of 67, there's plenty for him to find.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old in excellent nick with three wins from her last four starts on good ground, all at around the right distance; Jim Goldie has a solid recent strike rate and Lauren Young has the clearest tactical brief in the race — make the running and don't be caught — and the fast ground suits her confirmed style.|
runners_data.comment: This gelding ran up a hat-trick before that sequence ended, and a return to that level would make him hard to hold out, especially as he won here previously off a lower mark than his current 148 lb, and he's drawn in stall four this time. Rated 71, the obvious threat to that is a repeat of the notably faster ground that undid him last time, conditions that look on the cards again today.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Placed at 1m4f and 1m3f on good ground in recent starts and handled soft previously; Joanna Mason is an experienced conditional who rides the trip well, the trainer has limited recent form data (0 from 1 over 14 days) but the mare's profile makes her the most credible hold-up threat in the field.|
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency without a win in her last five starts, this mare confirmed she retains her form when only beaten 3 1/4 lengths off a 1lb higher mark at Catterick last time, and she's proven over today's trip and ground. Top-rated at 78, she looks the one to be positive about, with any doubt centred on her attitude under pressure.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Good-ground performer with a placed effort at 1m4f on good going, but this is a true hold-up horse who has been pushed forward in the race map because the rear is over-populated — the 0 wins and 0 places from 15 runs in similar going is a stark figure, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations even in a favourable scenario.|
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency who was only beaten two lengths at the Curragh last time, this gelding steps up today with a first-time tongue-tie that could sharpen him further. He's yet to convert that form into a win in his last five starts, but effective from 9 to 12 furlongs on a sound surface and rated 72, he's clearly one of this race's leading dangers.

runners_data.name: V Twelve
runners_data.note: Had 87 days off before a recent comeback run 56 days ago, and the layoff combined with a form string that includes a pulled-up effort over 22f suggests stamina reliability is uncertain; the horse's natural style is hold-up and, like Covert Legend, is mapped to midfield only because there is nowhere else to place it — treat its chances in any lead or prominent scenario with scepticism.|
runners_data.comment: This gelding has posted a win and two thirds among his last five starts, form that keeps him firmly in the mix at a rating of 60 from stall three under 144 lb. The obvious concern is finding that level again, having been well beaten after a switch to fences most recently, following a moderate effort on the level before that.

races.paceDynamic: Alpine Sierra is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she will be allowed to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m3f at Carlisle. The hold-up contingent — Junkyard Dog, Valley Of Flowers, Covert Legend and V Twelve — will all be racing from behind a single pace-setter, meaning the complexion of the race depends entirely on whether Alpine Sierra's fractions are slow enough to leave a finish or fast enough to win outright. Covert Legend and V Twelve are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with true closers; in reality, neither is likely to press Alpine Sierra for the early lead. This race shape — a lone, unhurried front-runner on fast ground over a stamina trip with a pack of hold-up horses trailing — strongly favours either Alpine Sierra herself if her rider controls tempo, or the most powerful and reliable closer who can pick her off in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpine Sierra Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra is allowed to bowl along uncontested and her rider sets a comfortable gallop that is never truly tested.
scenarios.body: If Alpine Sierra is allowed to bowl along uncontested and her rider sets a comfortable gallop that is never truly tested.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra sets a strong enough gallop that she ties up in the final furlong and the hold-up horses devour her.
scenarios.body: If Alpine Sierra sets a strong enough gallop that she ties up in the final furlong and the hold-up horses devour her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Valley Of Flowers Stalks And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Valley Of Flowers travels smoothly just off the pace and produces a sustained challenge that overpowers Alpine Sierra inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Valley Of Flowers travels smoothly just off the pace and produces a sustained challenge that overpowers Alpine Sierra inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Deliver Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and a reshuffle through the field allows Covert Legend or V Twelve to emerge from their unnatural midfield position and win on raw ability.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely and a reshuffle through the field allows Covert Legend or V Twelve to emerge from their unnatural midfield position and win on raw ability.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra's early position is the fulcrum of the entire race — if Lauren Young allows even one other runner to share the lead, the pace dynamic shifts and Alpine Sierra's chance diminishes sharply.

V Twelve's 87-day absence before a recent return run 56 days ago makes fitness hard to assess; watch the paddock for signs of condition, as a fresh horse operating out of role in midfield could be unpredictable.
Junkyard Dog's declining form string (5-4-5-8-9) suggests confidence should be tempered despite the 5lb claim from Cara Tuke — if the pace is genuinely slow, closers may never get competitive.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed across the card at Carlisle today — all runners show good-ground form entries, but Valley Of Flowers' most recent similar-going run was a placed effort over this trip, making her worth monitoring as the race develops in the straight.

With four hold-up horses chasing a single front-runner, watch for traffic issues in the straight — Carlisle's run-in can cause bunching if Alpine Sierra slows significantly, potentially costing one of the closers a clear run.

races.name: Caledonia Park Stylish Stayers Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Won four of her last seven starts including consecutive victories at 2m1f and 2m on good ground, making her a natural fit for this trip and surface; visor retained, Joanna Mason partners her, and a 16-day turnaround is no concern — the lone front-runner role is the entire story here, and her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she races slightly out of her most prominent position but her record says she handles it comfortably.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive with a hat-trick of wins before a good second last time under a 3lb rise, this mare is the one to beat on our figures. She's proven over today's trip and ground, tries a first-time visor, though her modest speed figure is the one query.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted and seven years old, she has placed just twice from 15 starts on similar going and lacks a win from four attempts on good ground, though her prominent style makes her the most natural beneficiary if Laravie can be caught; John Berry's stable has had a quiet 14 days (0/3) and the form string 446453 suggests consistency without a big effort imminent.|
runners_data.comment: Generally in good form, with a third beaten 5 1/4 lengths in a Kempton handicap last time, this gelding is clearly suited by this longer trip. He ranks second of six on our figures and tries first-time blinkers, though his modest speed figure is the one query.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's yard is in solid form (8/47 over 14 days) and this seven-year-old mare has form figures of 1-1-2-3 in her last four completed runs, suggesting she is in excellent shape; hood worn, she prefers soft ground based on her best efforts, so the good-to-firm conditions are the primary query, though she has won on good and the 21-day gap is not excessive.|
runners_data.comment: A dual winner this term, including a 6 1/2-length success off a lower mark two starts back, this gelding backed that up with a creditable third last time. He's proven on this ground and ranks third of six on our figures, but today's trip may stretch him beyond his best 12-16f range.

runners_data.name: Rupert The Prince
runners_data.note: Decent placed form at 2m1f on good ground (second of 12 runners in June) and is the youngest runner at four years old, but the key context is that this horse is a genuine prominent racer who the field map has absorbed into midfield — he won't find his natural position easily and that positional compromise will test his ability to produce his best; Rebecca Menzies has had only 2 wins from 20 runners in 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort for no obvious reason in a Pontefract handicap last time was a big letdown after a promising campaign that included a win and a narrow second. He's proven at today's trip and ground, but he's a modest contender on our figures even with a first-time visor to try.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's runner wears a tongue-tie and pads for the first time (tp headgear), returning just nine days after his last run — the most recent of any runner in this field; his true running style is hold-up or prominent, but he's been absorbed into midfield by the redistribution process, and his form figures of 740-65 along with a sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 15 gives little confidence in a big showing.|
runners_data.comment: Held comfortably in a Hamilton handicap last time on a trip that didn't suit, this gelding wants further and has at least dropped a long way in the weights. He's proven at today's trip and ground, but he's the bottom-rated runner here and remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Arctic Fox
runners_data.note: The veteran at ten years old brings a record of three places from 10 starts on good ground without a win, and a 19-day gap is routine; she is a genuine hold-up type whose best recent form (second, third) has come at shorter trips around 14f, making the 2m1f trip a stamina question, though she has run creditably over 16f and the quick surface appears manageable.|
runners_data.comment: Typically a picture of consistency racing off a fair mark, this mare looks overdue an upturn after a well-beaten run for no obvious reason here last time. She's proven at today's trip, handles cut in the ground, and ranks fourth of six on our figures, making her one to note on a return to form.

races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, is set to control this 2m1f contest at a measured, sustainable tempo on good-to-firm ground. Tarbat Ness will look to track close behind in second, while Cascade Hall, Arctic Fox, and the redistributed types settle into the rear half of the small six-runner field. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate — Rupert The Prince and Animato are natural prominent or hold-up runners who are unlikely to secure their preferred early position, meaning Laravie should dictate entirely unchallenged. A solo front-runner controlling a modest gallop over an extended trip on quick ground is a textbook scenario for the lead to be decisive, and horses that can travel close to the pace without expending energy — or produce a sustained rather than sharp late finish — are the profiles most favoured by this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Laravie Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Laravie bowls along at her own rhythm with no rival willing or able to press her into an uncomfortable early pace.
scenarios.body: If Laravie bowls along at her own rhythm with no rival willing or able to press her into an uncomfortable early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Laravie's lead is sustainable but one of the closers travels powerfully into contention and outstays her in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Laravie's lead is sustainable but one of the closers travels powerfully into contention and outstays her in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just fast enough to take the edge off the leaders and the field bunches, allowing a hold-up horse to pick them off late.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is just fast enough to take the edge off the leaders and the field bunches, allowing a hold-up horse to pick them off late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Laravie struggles to maintain her role or something forces an unexpected slow burn that turns this into a sprint finish for all.
scenarios.body: If Laravie struggles to maintain her role or something forces an unexpected slow burn that turns this into a sprint finish for all.

watchPoints.text: Laravie's ability to control fractions without a pacemaker rival is the race's single biggest factor — if she gets loose and comfortable, the race could be won before the straight.|

Cascade Hall's going preference leans soft; watch how she moves through the race on good-to-firm Carlisle ground, as any sign of not travelling freely would sharply reduce her chance of landing a late blow.|

Rupert The Prince and Animato are both natural prominent types forced to race off a slower position than they'd choose — if either pushes forward aggressively to find their preferred spot early, it could inject an unexpected injection of pace that disrupts Laravie's rhythm.|

Arctic Fox is ten years old and Carlisle's undulating track with a stiff finish adds a fitness and stamina premium — watch whether she comes off the bridle turning for home, which would signal she's feeling the distance.|

Tarbat Ness has blinkers on and is the horse most likely to close the gap on Laravie if she tracks her throughout; watch whether Gina Mangan elects to press or sit just off the leader, as that positional decision in the first half-mile will shape how the race is run.|

races.name: Caledonia Park Designer Dash Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer who has faded to finish positions of 9th, 10th and 15th in recent sprints; Nigel Tinkler has had no winners from 23 runners in the past 14 days and the ⚠ fade flag suggests she struggles to sustain her effort over the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Showed a clear step forward when second at Doncaster last time, beaten a length and a quarter off a marginally lower mark after five winless starts. Our top-rated runner on 85, well suited by today's trip and going, and the one to beat despite sitting below the level of his last success.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Soft recently (1/6f/SOF) which is a strong form line, but Lauren Young will need to coax her up from a hold-up position in a race that may not produce the strong pace she needs; only three comparable-going runs in the sample.
runners_data.comment: A head-verdict maiden success at Ayr last time marked a big leap forward from an educational debut, coming over today's trip on soft ground. That level of form has yet to be confirmed, though, and our figures leave him at the foot of this field on 62.

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 6f/GOO in her last five runs (4/6f/GOO, 4/6f/GOO) giving her the most consistent form profile among the closers; Charlie Johnston's yard is active at 6/47 in the past 14 days, and Joanna Mason is an experienced claimer who manages hold-up horses well in this type of contest.
runners_data.comment: Continued a run of steady efforts when beaten two lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Hamilton last time, though still winless in his last six starts. Racing off a fair weight and proven over today's trip, he's second on our figures at 79 and the main threat, but needs more to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Lumenbourg
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter who should get an uncontested bowl on Good to Firm ground she handles (twice placed at 6f/GOO); her visor (hg:v) aids concentration in front, and while her STYLE_FIT flag notes she is marginally racing out of role relative to the map, she is emphatically the natural leader here — her chance is enhanced, not diminished, by the absence of pace rivals.
runners_data.comment: A fair reflection of current form when fourth, beaten two and a quarter lengths off the same mark last time, with a win among his last five starts. Suited by today's trip and going and sporting a first-time visor, he sits only mid-pack on our figures at 70 despite the recent upturn.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Genuinely progressive at 6f/GOO, recording a course-distance win (1/6f/GOO) and a third on the same surface in recent form; her true running style is hold-up, pushed forward to midfield on the map purely by weight of numbers — Josephine Gordon's experience is an asset but the out-of-role placement tempers confidence about getting a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Third beaten two lengths off an identical mark last time, a fair effort in keeping with her level, with a win in her last six starts. Effective over today's trip on quick ground, she sits third in our figures on 78 and rates a leading threat, though she'll need more than a repeat effort to prevail.

runners_data.name: Sherlock
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's gelding has an excellent prominent profile — four of five recent runs at 6f/GOO produced placed finishes — and his hood (hg:b) tends to sharpen his early jump; he has the clearest racing style to sit second and pounce on Lumenbourg, making him the most dangerous rival under the dominant shape.
runners_data.comment: Racked up a pair of runner-up efforts among his last six starts, the latest coming at Hamilton when second, beaten two and a quarter lengths off an unchanged mark. First-time blinkers and a quick nine-day turnaround add interest, and he rates a leading danger on our figures at 70, even without a win to his name and with the yard out of sorts of late.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends out a high volume of runners (7/98 in 14 days) and Fan Mail has been consistent without winning, placing at 2/6f/SOF and 5/6f/GOO; her natural rear-of-field style means she has been mapped to midfield only by redistribution, and a modest pace limits her finishing opportunity.
runners_data.comment: Consistently below his best of late, without a win in his last six starts, and used up too soon when beaten five and a half lengths in a handicap at Ripon last time. First-time cheekpieces may help sharpen him up over his favoured trip, but he needs a definite improvement and sits only seventh on our figures at 66.

runners_data.name: Too Much
runners_data.note: Has been placed on Good-type ground twice over shorter trips (3/5f/GOO) but her OR of 58 is the second lowest in the race and her trainer has no wins from seven runners in 14 days; a true hold-up horse moved forward on the map by redistribution, and her record of 0W/1P in comparable going conditions is thin.
runners_data.comment: Failed to fire on soft ground when beaten five lengths in a handicap at this course last time, continuing a spell out of sorts without a win in her last five starts. She does have course form and acts well on quicker ground, which today's surface may suit better, leaving her a workable sixth on our figures at 69.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's filly has consistently finished mid-to-rear (best recent effort 5/6f/GOO) and the bulk of her history is at longer trips on softer surfaces; she is a genuine hold-up type appearing in midfield only because the map is crowded at the rear, and the fast conditions are an additional concern.
runners_data.comment: Struggling to find any consistency, without a win in her last six starts, she matched her recent level when beaten five lengths in a handicap at Pontefract last time. First-time cheekpieces offer some hope of sharpening her up over a trip and surface that suit, but she remains below the level she showed earlier this year and is only eighth on our figures at 64.

races.paceDynamic: Lumenbourg is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner sprint and, crucially, faces no genuine rival for the lead — she should secure a comfortable, uncontested bowl from the front on Good to Firm ground over Carlisle's straight six. With no pace pressure to burn her out early, she is likely to set a steady-to-fair tempo that keeps the race well within herself heading into the final two furlongs. The field is unusually stacked with hold-up types — Invincible Ruby, Fan Mail, Too Much and Maui Breeze are all true rear-of-field horses redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are more genuine closers than the race shape can accommodate at the back; Josephine Gordon on Invincible Ruby is most likely to actually press from a tracking position given her recent course-distance win profile, while Sherlock can also sit handy from his natural prominent style. This race shape heavily favours either the uncontested front-runner Lumenbourg or a horse who can race prominently just off the pace and pounce in the final furlong — deep closers relying on a strong gallop to reel in the leader face a structurally difficult task if the tempo is allowed to remain moderate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lumenbourg Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lumenbourg breaks cleanly and is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured pace throughout the six furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Lumenbourg breaks cleanly and is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured pace throughout the six furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Lumenbourg in second or third position has enough in reserve to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a horse tracking Lumenbourg in second or third position has enough in reserve to collar her inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Cut Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lumenbourg's uncontested lead is faster than it appears and sets up an unusually strong pace that unravels late.
scenarios.body: If Lumenbourg's uncontested lead is faster than it appears and sets up an unusually strong pace that unravels late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that the race turns into a sprint from the two-furlong pole with the entire field in contention.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is so slow that the race turns into a sprint from the two-furlong pole with the entire field in contention.

watchPoints.text: Lumenbourg's sectionals in the early stages — if she bowls along entirely unchallenged through the first two furlongs, her energy conservation advantage over the redistributed hold-up horses becomes decisive and the race is likely over long before the line.

Invincible Ruby's position at the start — Josephine Gordon may attempt to push her forward earlier than usual to overcome the redistribution disadvantage, and if she does track Lumenbourg in second it materially improves her chance beyond what the map suggests.

Sherlock's hood effect — he has worn the hood (hg:b) and produced prominent-tracking efforts repeatedly at 6f/GOO; if he breaks smartly under Taryn Langley he becomes the single most credible threat to Lumenbourg inside the final furlong.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 6f contest, matching the majority of Lumenbourg's and Sherlock's best form; closers whose best efforts came on Soft (Thistle Nil 1/6f/SOF, Too Much 3/8f/SOF) may find the faster surface less forgiving at the end of an evening card.

Fan Mail and Too Much are true hold-up horses buried in midfield by redistribution — monitor whether either jockey (Laura Pearson, Gina Mangan) attempts to ride against type to avoid traffic; if they do, it will likely compromise their finishing effort rather than improve it.
